speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: asked	the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (a) whether he can provide an update on the feedback received on Earn and Learn Programmes (ELP) in 2016; (b) whether the Ministry has been able to place 400 polytechnic and ITE graduates across all ELPs in 2016; and (c) which are the most sought after ELPs and whether they match existing manpower projections of the Industry Transformation Maps.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: The Ministry of Education will continue to work with the respective sector agencies to introduce more work-learn programmes to support training and lifelong learning.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The trainers, even the lecturers, have a close engagement with the students and participants and, at the end of it, they would also obtain feedback from the participants.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also work with the companies to see how we can get feedback and, at the same time, to better and improve the service delivery of the training institutes, as well as how we can enhance the learning experience of the participants.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is a developmental process whereby we make sure that what they learn is also linked to what they are doing at their workplace.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is not only about looking at what they have learnt, but also what they are going to do, what they are doing and, at the same time, we cannot run away from the fact that there are certain basic things that we need to remind them and to link these to what they had learnt before.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is an integral and integrated process whereby we want to manage the whole process of learning seamlessly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Will the Ministry consider, in the upcoming ELPs, allowing greater parity and for pay to catch up with market conditions?
